test_intent: Verifies that UserIndex.TryFindUserIdByUsername returns the correct userId when a matching cache entry exists.
reason: Test is fundamentally broken: it writes a synthetic cache value 'Message from @testuser1' with key '123456_789012', but production populates the cache via IndexUser(chatId, userId, messageText) where value is raw message text. The test passes only because the string 'testuser1' happens to be a substring of 'Message from @testuser1', not because it exercises the real production flow. The UserIndex is a thin wrapper around global MemoryCache.Default with no distinct bot contract beyond the general happy path. The global static cache makes tests fragile and non-isolated. No replacement needed because the real integration of IndexUser+TryFindUserId is exercised at the UserManager/UserManagement seam.

test_intent: Verifies that UserIndex.TryFindUserIdByUsername returns null when no cache entry matches the username.
reason: Same broken cache setup as the existing-user test: writes a synthetic cache entry for a different user, then asserts null for a non-matching username. The test passes trivially because the username doesn't appear in any cache value. This is a negative case that adds no value since the default return of the method is null. The global static MemoryCache makes the test fragile and non-isolated. No replacement needed because the null-default behavior is trivial and covered implicitly by the integration of IndexUser+TryFindUserId at the UserManagement seam.

test_intent: Verifies that UserIndex.TryFindUserIdByUsername performs case-insensitive username matching using StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase.
reason: The case-insensitive search behavior (StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase at line 20 of UserIndex.cs) is a real production contract worth preserving. The current test is broken: it writes cache value 'Message from @testuser3' then searches for 'testuser3' (lowercased in both places), so it never actually exercises case-insensitive matching. The test should write a value with one case and search with a different case to verify OrdinalIgnoreCase behavior. Additionally, the cache setup uses synthetic values instead of the production IndexUser flow. Rewrite as a focused unit test on UserIndex with proper case mismatch between indexed value and search query, e.g., index 'MESSAGE FROM @ADMIN' and search for 'admin'.
